input.quote: 9.6 Late Payments. If a Party does not receive payment of any undisputed sum due to it on or before the due date therefor, then it shall notify the paying Party. The paying Party shall pay interest on any undisputed late payments (before and after any judgment) at an annual rate (but with interest accruing on a daily basis) of the lesser of (a) [***] percent above the London Interbank Offered Rate for deposits in Dollars having a maturity of one month published by the British Bankers' Association
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or minimum-fee provision payable by Sanofi (our party). Searches for "liquidated damages" and "penalty" return nothing; the financial provisions (Article IX) impose only upfront, milestone, royalty and profit/loss-share payments tied to actual performance, and the sole late-payment consequence is ordinary reciprocal interest at LIBOR + [***]% capped at the maximum lawful rate (Section 9.6), which the rule expressly treats as not a liquidated-damages deviation. Termination by Sanofi for convenience under Section 12.2(a)(i) requires only notice, with no early-termination or minimum fee; the post-termination royalty flow in Section 12.3(c)(ii)C runs from RevMed to Sanofi and so benefits us. For diligence failures under Section 5.7, Section 12.6 makes termination the exception to the "not sole remedy" rule rather than imposing a fixed sum. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted.
